findings.issue: Item 7's test An_entry_larger_than_the_manifest_declares_is_refused_without_buffering_it_whole only exercises ReadEntry (the ReadOne path). ExtractTo carries its own copy of the CopyWithLimit call and is never asserted, so a future edit that drops the limit on the disk-writing path would not be caught.
findings.fix: Extend the same test with a second assertion: call reader.ExtractTo(world.Folder.File("out"), ContainerKeySource.OfficeKey(officeKey)) on the same tampered container and assert Assert.Throws<CryptoException> with ErrorCode.Tampered.

findings.issue: Item 2 asks for a test per mismatch. The plain-field half of EnsureTrusted is covered only for Body.OrgId (An_answer_whose_plain_fields_disagree_with_its_own_certificate_is_refused), and the key half only by a single case that mismatches Ed25519Pub and X25519Pub together. A regression that dropped the OfficeId, PcDeviceId or X25519Pub comparison alone would still pass.
findings.fix: Turn both tests into [Theory] cases (or add three small facts) that mismatch exactly one field at a time: Body.OfficeId, Body.PcDeviceId, and a phone certificate whose Ed25519Pub matches but whose X25519Pub does not, each asserting ErrorCode.BadSignature.

findings.issue: Item 4 specified rejecting any character from Path.GetInvalidFileNameChars() other than '/'. The implementation instead hard-codes SegmentInvalidChars = ['"','<','>','|','*','?'] and relies on separate whole-name checks for '\\', ':' and control characters. On Windows that set is exactly equivalent, but the equivalence is implicit and would silently drift if the framework list changed or the code were ever compiled for another platform.
findings.fix: Replace the literal array with a static readonly char[] built once from Path.GetInvalidFileNameChars().Where(c => c != '/' && c != '\\').ToArray() (keeping the existing explicit '\\', ':' and control-character rules), so the predicate tracks the platform's own list.
